derivation: computed by waves/route.py from surfaces.json and plans.json
limits: It routes demand and does not measure absorption: how much of an entry Ravel's platform already answers needs a reader per entry, which this does not attempt.

Content behaviour is charged to every entry carrying class files, because the inventory does not distinguish a class that registers data from one that implements a block. That makes the content-behaviour figure an upper bound.

content-behaviour has a module and still reads False. A mod can now declare a block or an item, describe how it behaves, and have the host register it in a launched game — but a counterpart needs blocks that do something, and a block whose only behaviour is hardness, blast resistance, tool requirement and random ticking is not that. The flag flips when the surface carries behaviour a mod writes rather than values it picks.

A capability's reachesARunningGame verdict is written here by hand from what docs/guide/limits.md states in the public repository. It is a claim about the host at the time of writing and goes stale when the host gains a surface.
It reads the inventory's own counts and opens no artifact.
